status.en: 23 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 23% fewer than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Addis Ababa.
status.nb: 23 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 23 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Addis Ababa.

summary.en: In the past week 26 armed incidents were reported, 19% fewer than the previous week, mainly in Tigray, Amhara and Addis Ababa, with six incidents covered by multiple outlets. The UCDP recorded 2,824 battle‑related deaths in 2024. Reports describe Ethiopian drones striking Eritrean forces, accusations of Eritrean troops entering Ethiopian territory, and calls for UN intervention by both sides. Tensions are heightened by mutual accusations of incursions and declarations of self‑defence, while regional partners watch the standoff closely.
summary.nb: I løpet av den siste uken ble 26 væpnede hendelser rapportert, 19 % færre enn uken før, hovedsakelig i Tigray, Amhara og Addis Ababa, hvor seks hendelser ble dekket av flere kilder. UCDP registrerte 2 824 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024. Rapporter beskriver etiopiske droner som treffer eritreiske styrker, anklager om eritreiske tropper som går inn i etiopisk territorium, og oppfordringer til FN‑intervensjon fra begge sider. Spenningen øker med gjensidige beskyldninger om inntrengninger og selvforsvar, mens regionale partnere følger opptrinnet nøye.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
